zh: 本书的目标，是就我们所谓“拜占庭帝国”作为一个政治社会的性质，提出一个原创性的论点。在讨论拜占庭政治领域时，学界几乎只聚焦于皇帝，并倾向于照单全收宫廷常常宣称的那套为其权力合法性辩护的神学依据。我将论证，这幅图景是片面的，甚至是误导性的。拜占庭首先必须被理解为一个罗马传统意义上的共和国。正如我将在第一章解释的，我所谓“共和国”，指的是这样一种政体：唯有征得人民同意，才能授予权力，而权力只能用来增进全体罗马人民的福祉（也就是我们所谓的“拜占庭人”）。照此定义，共和国和君主制可以相容。直到启蒙时代，大多数政治理论家都持这种看法。相比之下，我们（而非罗马人）所谓的“共和国”（大写 Republic），不过是
或
在某一历史阶段采取的一种特定政体，其治理者是元老院、执政官和人民大会。拜占庭是广义上的共和国。罗马人民始终是政治领域真正的主权者，他们可以赋予统治者执掌权力的资格，也可以撤回这种资格。后者，即“罗马人的皇帝”，必须放在由罗马人民整体所构成的政治领域中来理解。
正是古代
的拜占庭希腊语翻译与延续。
en: The goal of this book is to present an original argument regarding the nature of what we call “the Byzantine empire” as a political society. In discussing the Byzantine political sphere, scholarship has focused almost exclusively on the emperor and has tended to accept at face value the theological grounds for the legitimacy of his power often claimed by the court. This picture, I will argue, is partial and even misleading. Byzantium must first be understood as a republic in the Roman tradition. As I will explain in Chapter 1, by “republic” I mean a regime in which only popular consent could authorize the allocation of power, which could be used only to benefit the totality of the Roman people (whom we call the “Byzantines”). According to this definition, and following most political theorists down to the Enlightenment, republics and monarchies were not incompatible. By contrast, what we (and not the Romans) call the “Republic” was only one specific type of regime by which the
or

was governed in one phase of its history, namely, by the senate, consuls, and popular assemblies. Byzantium was a republic in the broader sense. The Roman people remained the true sovereign of the political sphere, and they both authorized and de-authorized the holding of power by their rulers. The latter, “the emperors of the Romans,” must be understood in relation to the political sphere constituted by the totality of the Roman people. The
was the Byzantine Greek translation and continuation of the ancient

zh: 这项计划是一项双重努力的一部分，旨在恢复拜占庭的罗马维度，以及拜占庭人自身的罗马身份。作为续篇与姊妹篇的那本书，将依据史料证据以及自二十世纪中叶以来在社会科学与历史学中占主导地位的理论模型来论证：拜占庭人不仅“自称罗马人”（这是我们这个领域闪烁其词、勉勉强强的说法），而且实际上就是罗马人——诚然是说希腊语、信奉东正教的罗马人，但终究是罗马人。相比之下，本卷不聚焦于身份主张，而是运用政治理论以及拜占庭政治的独特框架来论证：处于拜占庭阶段的罗马人民，构成了一个轮廓清晰可辨为共和式的政治领域。在我的用法中（亦即追随罗马人的用法），“共和的”指的是作为政治基础的权力观念与人民主权观念；它与官职结构无关（“共和国”并不是罗马人对那个时期的称呼，而是一个现代术语，指一段时期和一种特定的治理方式）。
en: This project is part of a two-pronged effort to rehabilitate the Roman dimension of Byzantium and the Roman identity of the Byzantines themselves. The sequel and companion book will argue, according to both the evidence and theoretical models that have prevailed in the social and historical sciences since the mid-twentieth century, that the Byzantines not only “called themselves Romans” (as our field evasively and grudgingly puts it) but actually were that: Greek-speaking, Orthodox Christian Romans to be sure, but Romans still. The present volume, by contrast, will not focus on identity claims but will use political theory and the peculiar framework of Byzantine politics to argue that the Roman people in their Byzantine phase constituted a political sphere whose contours were recognizably republican. In my usage, which follows that of the Romans, “republican” refers to underlying ideologies of power and notions of popular sovereignty; it does not have to do with the structure of offices (“the Republic” was not called that by the Romans, but is a modern term for a period and a specific mode of governance).

zh: 乔治·奥斯特洛戈尔斯基撰写过一部通行的拜占庭国家史（初版于1952年），他无可非议地断言：“罗马政治概念、希腊文化与基督教信仰，是决定拜占庭发展的主要要素。”

然而，尽管学界普遍承认“罗马”与拜占庭有某种关联，却从未确切说明那究竟是什么。奥斯特洛戈尔斯基所指的那些“概念”是什么？问题部分源于拜占庭学作为一个研究领域的起源。在西欧，这项研究是在许多与罗马遗产有利害关系的政治和宗教机构划定的观念界限内进行的。自中世纪早期以来，拜占庭对罗马的主张就遭到拒绝，并在论战中被否认。拜占庭学领域把那场论战的主张当作显而易见的事实继承下来，于是不得不设法用不同于东罗马帝国自称的名称来称呼它。因此我们被强加了“希腊人的帝国”“君士坦丁堡的帝国”以及“拜占庭”这些称呼，因为照这种观点，真正的罗马属于拉丁语的西方。可是罗马与罗马的主张在拜占庭证据中比比皆是。鉴于学界极不情愿承认拜占庭人
罗马人，这些证据被以两种方式之一加以解释。第一种，是把那些罗马概念等同于凯撒利亚主教优西比乌应用于君士坦丁大帝的那套帝国神学。这实际上把拜占庭的罗马成分归入了基督教成分；许多顶尖历史学家今天仍坚持拜占庭是基督教的
罗马的，
而不是说它两者皆是、只是方式不同。于是奥斯特洛戈尔斯基的三根支柱被缩减为两根。据最近一本著作所说，“人们也习惯于把拜占庭文化视为建立在两个要素之上：希腊的……以及犹太—基督教传统。”
另一种解释把罗马成分视为皇权宣传的产物，认为它仅见于头衔和外交。
它残存在这样一种看法中：拜占庭人之所以是罗马人，是因为他们是皇帝的臣民，仿佛他们纵有罗马身份，也是从皇帝的头衔得来的（事实恰恰相反）。
en: George Ostrogorsky, who wrote a standard history of the Byzantine state (first published in 1952), unobjectionably claimed that “Roman political concepts, Greek culture, and the Christian faith were the main elements that determined Byzantine development.”

But while the field generally concedes that “Rome” had something to do with Byzantium, it has never been specified exactly what that was. What were those “concepts” that Ostrogorsky referred to? Part of the problem stems from the origins of Byzantine Studies as a field of research. In western Europe, this research took place within the ideological parameters set by many political and religious institutions that had a stake in the Roman legacy. Since early medieval times the Byzantine claim to Rome had been rejected and polemically denied. The field of Byzantine Studies inherited the claims of that polemic as obvious facts and so had to devise ways of referring to the eastern Roman empire that were different from what it called itself. Thus we have been saddled with “the empire of the Greeks,” “the empire of Constantinople,” and “Byzantium,” for Rome proper belonged to the (Latin) West. But Rome and Roman claims are written all over the Byzantine evidence. Given the extreme reluctance in the field to admit that the Byzantines

Romans, this evidence has been interpreted in one of two ways. The first is to equate those Roman concepts with the theology of empire applied by the bishop Eusebios of Kaisareia to Constantine the Great. This effectively folds the Roman dimension into the Christian one; many leading historians today still maintain that Byzantium was Christian
Roman,

not that it was both but in different ways. Thus Ostrogorsky’s three pillars have been reduced to two. According to a recent book, “it has also been common to regard Byzantine culture as based on two elements: the Greek... and the Judaic and Christian tradition.”
The other option is to regard the Roman aspect as a function of imperial propaganda, limited to titles and diplomacy.

It survives in the view that the Byzantines were Roman insofar as they were the subjects of the emperor, as if they derived their Roman identity, such as it was, from his title (the exact opposite was in fact true).

zh: 本书意在修正通说。它质疑既定见解，提出别的模型，以便更好地解释事实，也解释既有模型所回避的事实。为此，它不重复那些在别处已被重复得足够多的东西。想阅读把拜占庭作为一个东正教社会来论述的读者，应当另寻他书：那个主题的书并不缺乏。但在我看来，占主导地位的东正教模型不仅是片面的，而且是站不住脚的。因此，本书源于一个日益强烈的认识：大多数现代学术所描述的拜占庭，与人们在史料中遭遇的那个社会相背离，有时背离甚远。人们用一些多半是现代的概念，拼凑出一个公式化的“拜占庭政治理论”定义，把它投射到这种文化上，并自1930年代以来反复沿袭。学者们满足于背诵这个模型作为该文化的总体定义，然后才转去研究他们感兴趣的特定方面。后一种聚焦研究质量很高，但容纳它的那个总体框架却从未受到批判性审视。学界本应比现在更担忧的是：那些仍被当作拜占庭政治意识形态权威依据的基础研究，是由亲身应对二十世纪三十年代危机，或在那场危机中接受学术训练的欧洲学者写成的，而且他们推崇神权式的而非平民主义的政治意识形态。
en: This is a revisionist book: it aims to question established opinion and proposes alternative models that better explain the facts, or explain facts that established models avoid. To this end, it does not repeat things that are repeated often enough elsewhere. Readers who want to read about Byzantium as an Orthodox society should look elsewhere: there is no lack of books on that topic. But in my view the dominant Orthodox model is not only one-sided, it is not viable. This book, then, stems from a growing realization that the Byzantium described in most modern scholarship diverges from the society one encounters in the sources, sometimes widely. A formulaic definition of “Byzantine political theory” has been constructed out of mostly modern concepts, projected onto the culture, and recycled since the 1930s. Scholars are content to recite this model as a general definition of the culture before they move on to study the particular aspects that interest them. The latter focused research is of high quality, but the general framework into which it is pressed has never been subjected to critical scrutiny. The field ought to be more worried than it is that the basic studies that are still cited as authoritative for Byzantine political ideology were written by European scholars coping with, or trained in, the crisis of the 1930s, and that they valorized theocratic over populist political ideologies.

zh: 我们那幅关于拜占庭政治意识形态的“暗中支配的图景”
认定：皇帝与所谓的帝国理念——一种政治神学——在政治领域内部拥有绝对支配权，并且完全填满了这个政治领域；皇帝的地位是相对于上帝来理解、并由此获得合法性的。引用一位顶尖学者的话：“帝国由一种以宫廷及其首都君士坦丁堡为依托的强烈意识形态维系在一起。这种意识形态围绕两根轴心旋转：皇权与东正教。”
按照这一立场的大多数版本，“意识形态”在皇帝与上帝之间的一个形而上领域里展开，帝国臣民无缘参与其中，只能带着敬畏和顺从仰望它。历史学家过去也强调“皇帝的崇高地位，他支配并控制着帝国的全部生活……他所行使的权力是巨大的、无限的，且不服从任何更高权威。”
近期学术淡化了这种绝对主义，承认皇帝在实践中并非如此强大，其统治也不被臣民视为绝对，尽管皇权的基础仍被从宗教角度来理解。
en: Our “insidious governing image”

of Byzantine political ideology would have it that the emperor and the so-called imperial idea—a type of political theology—held absolute dominion within, and also completely filled up, the political sphere, and that the position of the emperor was understood and also legitimized in relation to God. To quote a leading scholar: “The empire was held together by a strong ideology based on its court and capital at Constantinople. This ideology revolved around two axes: the imperial power and the Orthodox religion.”

“Ideology,” according to most versions of this position, played out in a metaphysical realm between emperor and God to which imperial subjects had no access and upon which they gazed in awe and submission. Historians also used to stress “the exalted position of the emperor, who dominated and controlled the entire life of the empire... The power he wielded was vast, unlimited, and subject to no higher authority.”

Recent scholarship has played down this absolutism by recognizing that the emperor was not quite so powerful in practice and his rule was not recognized as absolute by his subjects, even though the foundations for imperial power are still understood in religious terms.

zh: 本书将捍卫一种替代性观点，它过去曾由汉斯-格奥尔格·贝克在1960与1970年代提出过，尽管是以初步且未充分展开的方式。本书将主张：拜占庭拥有一种复杂的政治文化，其中不同的意识形态体系相互叠加，一种是罗马的、共和的、世俗的，另一种是晚期罗马的、形而上的、并最终基督教化的，它们占据政治领域的不同位置。这本身并不是一个原创论题，
但本书还将论证：无论是在拜占庭人的意识形态方面，还是在他们政治领域的运作方面，历史学家都应把优先地位给予
成分。那套令学界目眩神迷太久的皇帝职位神学，应当被降格。我们不应仅仅、甚至主要地通过宗教来接近拜占庭政治。拜占庭事实上是罗马
的延续；其政治尽管制度有所变化，却仍持续被共和传统的意识形态模式与秩序所主导。这是贝克的伟大洞见，但他追随者寥寥，
他对证据的替代性解读也未成为学界采纳的分析或历史框架。问题部分在于：他与其说是发展了自己的论题，不如说是在几篇零散的文章与章节中勾勒了它，提供的文献佐证很少。
在我看来，他著作最大的弱点——正是这个弱点使得几乎无人领会他的意思——在于他没有明确挑战学界的主流观点，尽管他理解那些观点的缺陷，因而未能说明他所言对于其他学者就该主题的思考有何意义。结果，人们把他的论述放在一旁，当成对公认常识的又一次泛泛重述。于是他们得以把贝克同观点几乎与他相反的学者并列引用，仿佛两边说的是一回事，从而消解了他的观点与主流看法的冲突。这制造了学界一致与共识的虚假图景。
en: An alternative view will be defended here, one that has been proposed in the past, albeit in a preliminary and underdeveloped way, by Hans-Georg Beck in the 1960s and 1970s. This book will propose that Byzantium had a complex political culture in which different ideological systems were superimposed, one Roman, republican, and secular and the other late Roman, metaphysical, and eventually Christian, and they occupied different sites of the political sphere. In itself this is not an original thesis,
but it will also be argued here that priority in terms of both the ideology of the Byzantines and the functioning of their political sphere should be given by historians to the

component. The theology of the imperial office, which has dazzled the field for too long, should be demoted. We should not be approaching Byzantine politics exclusively or even primarily through religion. Byzantium was in fact the continuation of the Roman

and its politics, despite changes in institutions, continued to be dominated by the ideological modes and orders of the republican tradition. This was Beck’s great insight, but he found few followers,

and his alternate reading of the evidence has not been taken up by the field as an analytical or historical framework. Part of the problem is that he did not so much develop his thesis as sketch it in a few scattered articles and chapters, providing little documentation.

In my view the greatest weakness of his work, which ensured that few would grasp what he was saying, is that he did not explicitly challenge dominant views in the field, though he understood their flaws, and thus failed to explain the significance of what he was saying for what other scholars were thinking about the topic. As a result, he was folded into the background as yet another generic restatement of what everyone already knew. It thus became possible to tame Beck by citing him along with scholars who held more or less the opposite view, as if they were all saying the same thing. This creates a false image of unanimity and consensus in the field.

zh: 我们对拜占庭政治领域的理解，缺失了一个关键要素，而它在几乎所有原始史料中都占据显著位置：我指的是
概念——拉丁
的一个古代翻译——连同它的同源词与近义词（前现代术语在大多数文学或文献体裁中从来不是统一的）。贝克版本的共和论题之所以受损，也在于它未能揭示这个概念对拜占庭人的意义与核心地位，未能表明它对他们的政治思维与行为有多么根本，尽管他意识到它的重要性。作为政治领域的
，反映了罗马人民的共识，这共识运作于一个既涵盖皇帝、也涵盖皇帝所统治的那个共同体的概念空间之中。这个概念对拜占庭政治观的重要性不应被低估，然而它在我们对其文化的表述中完全缺席。本书试图恢复“个体用以在政治上为自己定向的那幅心智地图”，
首先揭示弥漫于多种体裁拜占庭文本中的关于政治的逻辑，尤其是法律文本、军事论著、史学及其他。这些文本每一种都从不同视角呈现并讨论同样的核心观念，使我们得以形成一幅完整的图景，并考察其中各方的利益。
en: Our understanding of the Byzantine political sphere is missing a crucial element that has a prominent place in almost all the primary sources: I mean the concept of the
an ancient translation of the Latin

along with its cognates and synonyms (premodern terminology never being uniform in most literary or documentary genres). Beck’s version of the republican thesis suffered also because it failed to bring out the meaning and centrality for the Byzantines of this concept, to show how fundamental it was for their political thinking and behavior, though he was aware of its importance. The

as a political sphere reflected the consensus of the Roman people that operated in a conceptual space that encompassed both the emperor and the community of whom he was the emperor. The importance of this concept should not be underestimated for the Byzantine view of politics, and yet it is entirely missing from our representation of their culture. This book seeks to restore “the mental map by which individuals oriented themselves politically,”

first by revealing the logic about politics that pervades Byzantine texts in many genres, especially legal texts, military treatises, historiography, and others. Each of these presents and discusses the same core ideas, albeit from a different viewpoint, which enables us to form a rounded picture and to consider the interests of different parties within it.

zh: 在首先考量意识形态框架之后，我将在第五章转而考察

在历史上如何实际运作。只有在最后一章（第六章），我才会考量罗马与基督教意识形态的互动，因为我将论证：我们迄今为止视为政治领域之定义性特征的东西——神权式帝国理念——其实是宫廷的一种尝试，要用修辞来缓解它在治理一个动荡共和国时始终所处的脆弱地位。因此，本书大部分篇幅将致力于按其自身逻辑呈现后一模型，看看我们能用它解释哪些政治现象与话语。只有到最后，我才会退后一步，考量拜占庭多种权力话语的更广阔语境。
en: After considering first the ideological framework, I will turn to the

as a historical entity in action (in Chapter 5). Only in the final chapter (Chapter 6) will the interaction of Roman and Christian ideologies be considered, for I will argue that what we have so far taken to be definitive of the political sphere—the theocratic imperial idea—was an attempt by the court to ameliorate rhetorically the vulnerable position in which it found itself always in managing a turbulent republic. Most of the book will, therefore, be devoted to presenting the latter model on its own terms, to see what political phenomena and discourses we can explain by it. Only at the end will I step back to consider the broader context of multiple discourses of power in Byzantium.

zh: 尽管
在学术中被抹去了，它在史料中却无处不在。正因如此，我大量引用史料原文，并把希腊文放在注释里、有时放在正文中。在讨论某一特定史料的内容时，我使用转写形式
，但在我自己的论述中有时使用“政体”（polity）一词；出于将会变得清楚的理由，我常常使用最接近的直接翻译“共和国”（republic）。作为一个英语词，“政体”（polity）没有
一词所带的联想（该词因英联邦和奥博连斯基虚构的“拜占庭邦联”而有了复杂的含义，两者都和
原来的意思相去甚远）；
也不意味着“国家”（state）——而它常被译作“国家”，其后果有时是灾难性的。
en: While the

has been effaced in the scholarship, it is pervasive in the sources. For this reason I cite many quotations from the sources and place the Greek in the notes and sometimes in the text. I use the transliterated form

when discussing the contents of a particular source but sometimes use the form “polity” in my own exposition; I often use the closest direct translation, “republic,” for reasons that will become clear. As an English word, “polity” does not carry the baggage of “commonwealth” (complicated by the British Commonwealth and Obolensky’s fictitious Byzantine Commonwealth, both worlds apart from what
meant), nor does
mean “state,” which is how it is often translated, with consequences that are sometimes disastrous.

zh: “帝国”（empire）是另一个令人困惑的术语，它也未被充分理论化。我就拜占庭而言使用“帝国”，意思是它由一位我们约定俗成称为皇帝的统治者治理，实质上是一位君主，即罗马人的

。换言之，在我的用法中“帝国”意味着“君主制”，我对学者们赋予这个词的其他含义暂且持怀疑态度。例如，另一种做法是因为它对非罗马人施加帝国统治而称其为帝国——它有时确实如此——但这有滑入“多族群帝国”概念的危险，而就拜占庭而言我对这个概念持怀疑态度。后者是一个误导性的概念，它有意或无意地瓦解并抹去了“帝国”绝大多数人口的（罗马）同质性。遗憾的是，我们用同一个词来指称如此不同的方面（即拥有“皇帝”与作为一个多族群帝国），而这两者并不总是重合。它们的确在早期罗马帝国重合（我们所用的
和
就源于那里），但在拜占庭，重合的程度较低。
这些问题我将在本研究的续篇中更充分探讨。
en: “Empire” is another confusing term, which has also been inadequately theorized. By “empire” in relation to Byzantium I mean that it was governed by a ruler whom we conventionally call an emperor, in effect a monarch, the

of the Romans. In other words, in my usage “empire” means “monarchy,” and I remain provisionally skeptical of other senses that are attributed to the word by scholars. For example, an alternative would be to call it an empire because it exerted imperial dominion over non-Romans, which at times it did, but this poses the danger of sliding into the concept of the “multiethnic empire,” about which I am skeptical in the case of Byzantium. The latter is a misleading concept that intentionally or not disintegrates and elides the (Roman) homogeneity of the vast majority of the population of the “empire.” It is unfortunate that we use the same term to refer to such different aspects (namely, having an “emperor” and being a multiethnic empire), which did not always coincide. They did coincide in the early Roman empire, where our terms “imperium” and “imperator” originate, but less so in Byzantium.
These are issues that I will explore more fully in the sequel to this study.

zh: 由于本书将呈现一个与大多数通论和专门研究中所见相当不同的拜占庭，论证必须分步骤展开。每一步都不可能把所有旁支问题提出来一一考察，否则会打断论述，生出许多枝节，其中有些本就可以单独成题。我希望每位读者的一般关切能在论证的后续部分得到回应，但我知道一开始不可能涵盖一切。
en: As this book will present a Byzantium considerably different from what is found in most surveys and specialized studies, the argument must be presented in steps. Not every lateral problem can be identified and examined at each step, for that would break up the exposition and create many digressions, some of which are separate topics in their own right. I hope that the general concerns of each reader are addressed at a later point in the argument, but I know that it will not be possible to cover everything at first.

zh: 按惯例应当以学术史回顾开篇，但在本例中那将包括历史学家就拜占庭所写的大多数泛论性著作。我就得写一部

了。虽然我们迫切需要那样一部书，但它无法在此处、也无法由我来完成。至少可以说这一点：我试图纠正的关于拜占庭的大多数误解，是早在今天尚在世的学者出生以前就已形成。今天的学者也许有他们自己重复这些误解的理由，但它们不是他们发明的。然而，我们关于拜占庭的这些核心观念，起初并不是由严谨的学术方法确立的，从未真正被“证明”过，在现代也未受到批判性审视。其中一些，包括对拜占庭人罗马身份的否认，是从学术出现之前的时代传给我们的，其起源与政治和宗教利益相连——只要我们了解这些利益，作为历史学家我们就会与之划清界限。我希望，尽管我们已对这些观念习以为常，我们对维持这些观念却没有切身利益。从许多会议经历中，我感觉到学界已准备好开始探索拜占庭的罗马维度，走出对罗马之名的恐惧，以及“对基督教的痴迷与……一心一意的聚焦”。
en: It is customary to begin with a review of the scholarship, but in this case that would include most of what has been written by historians about Byzantium in general terms. I would have to write a

While we desperately need that, it cannot be done here or by me. It is at least possible to say this. Most of the misunderstandings about Byzantium that I seek to correct were set in place before the lifetime of any scholar now alive. Scholars today may have their own reasons for repeating them, but they did not invent them. These core notions of ours about Byzantium, however, were not established by rigorous scholarly methods to begin with, were never actually “proven,” and have not been subjected to critical scrutiny in modern times. Some, including the denial of the Byzantines’ Roman identity, have been handed down to us from ages before the emergence of academic scholarship, and their origins are linked to political and religious interests that we would disown as historians, if only we knew of them. It is my hope that while we have grown comfortable with these notions, we also have no personal stake in them. From many experiences at conferences I gain the sense that the field is ready to begin exploring the Roman dimension of Byzantium, to move past the horror of the Roman name and the “obsession and... single-minded focus on Christianity.”

zh: 本书会引用一些我所反对的观点的代表人物。这些观点大多如此普遍，以至于可以从数十乃至数百种现代出版物中举例说明。它们是学界每个人都曾一度持有过的立场，我自己也包括在内。我通常尽量引用学界顶尖学者的著作，我极为尊重他们。但正如我上面解释的，他们不是这些立场的最初倡导者，只是其现代承载者。有时我几乎随机地引用出版物，因为这些立场几乎随处可见。所以如果你在注释中看到自己的名字，请明白那（通常）本可以是任何其他人。如上所述，大多数拜占庭学者研究具体问题并产出卓越成果。我的靶子是我们用来界定该文化及其政治意识形态的那些宽泛抽象。今天没有谁该为它们负责，尽管我们都延续了它们。
en: In the course of this book, I will be citing exponents of views with which I disagree. Most of these views are so pervasive that they could be illustrated from dozens or hundreds of modern publications. They are positions that everyone in the field has held at one time or another, myself included. I generally try to cite the works of leading scholars in the field, whom I respect immensely. But, as I explained above, they are not the original exponents of these positions, only their modern carriers. Sometimes I cite publications almost at random, since these positions can be found almost everywhere. So if you see your name in the notes, please know that it (usually) could have been anyone else. As I said above, most Byzantinists work on specific issues and produce excellent results. My targets are the broad abstractions that we use to define the culture and its political ideology. No one today is responsible for them, though we have all perpetuated them.

zh: 本书的论证将取材于公元五世纪晚期至十二世纪。起点以皇帝们定都君士坦丁堡为标志，也标志着自三世纪开始的流动的军事统治一度打断这段历史之后，以人民为重的共和规范重新发挥作用。论证本可以仅以拜占庭中期的材料为基础，但我想表明这些传统如何扎根于古代晚期的罗马。正如沃尔特·凯吉所指出的，“许多学者不愿把他们对七、八世纪的研究与对五、六世纪的研究结合起来，致使许多本可说清楚的问题变得难以理解。”
我并不是说拜占庭共和国在五世纪突然出现，然后在十字军摧毁它时又同样突然地消失。它的历史实际上向上可追溯至罗马共和国，往下又延续至1453年，那条漫长轨迹的某些方面将沿途呈现。
历史并不总是按照学术分界展开。但把论证充分延伸到那两个方向会使它不必要地复杂化；那需要进一步讨论其错综复杂的兴衰。公元500—1200年这一段已有足够的材料可供处理。
en: The argument in the book will draw on material from the late fifth century to the twelfth. The starting point is marked by the settling of the emperors in Constantinople and the dynamic resumption of populist republican norms after the intermission of itinerant military rule that started in the third century. The argument could have been based on material from the middle Byzantine period alone, but I wanted to show how these traditions were anchored in Roman late antiquity. As Walter Kaegi pointed out, “the reluctance of many scholars to combine their investigations of the seventh and eighth centuries with researches on the fifth and sixth centuries has contributed to an unnecessary obfuscation of many topics.”

I am not arguing that the Byzantine republic appeared suddenly in the fifth century and then just as suddenly disappeared when the Crusaders destroyed it. Its history actually extends back into the Roman Republic and forward to 1453, and aspects of that long trajectory will be presented along the way.

History did not unfold always according to academic boundaries. But extending the argument fully in those two directions would complicate it unnecessarily; it would require further discussions of its messy rise and fall. There is enough to work within the period 500–1200.

zh: 本书的论证难免会被指责没有突出这一时期可能发生的种种变化，指责它呈现了一个一成不变的拜占庭的铁板一块的图景。然而我的目标是界定一条基线，据此变化才能被识别和解释。鉴于过去把这种文化视为锁定在永恒衰落中的看法，拜占庭学者们理所当然地拥抱了“变化”的口号，但有时似乎是为变化而变化。拜占庭社会具有罕见的一贯性。我们往往把它在史料中如此容易辨认当作理所当然，却忘了它的文化与社会同一种特定政治秩序联系得多么紧密。我所寻找的，正是那种身份与连续性的基本参数，而我坚持认为，这些参数随时间变化甚微。在这个根本层面上缺乏变化，过去常被当作永久衰落的标志，但我把它视为动态稳定的证明与力量的源泉。
en: The argument will inevitably be faulted for not highlighting changes that may have taken place during this period, for presenting a monolithic picture of an unchanging Byzantium. My goal, however, is to define the baseline against which changes can be identified and interpreted. Given past views of the culture as locked in timeless decadence, Byzantinists have understandably embraced the slogan of change, but sometimes it seems to be for its own sake. Byzantium was a remarkably coherent society. We take for granted how easy it is to recognize in the source-record and forget how tied its culture and society were to a specific political order. What I am looking for are precisely the basic parameters of that identity and continuity, and these, I maintain, changed little over time. Lack of change on this fundamental level used to be taken as a sign of permanent decadence, but I take it as proof of dynamic stability and a source of strength.
